correctness.rationale: The kernel normalization follows from exact normalized edge-second moments; vertex localization follows from convexity and a strict sign-disagreement argument. The negative interval of vertices J through n-J is established by an explicit trigonometric inequality. Two crossing-edge deficit triangles yield the exact formula. Uniform Taylor expansions of a sine quotient and a rational crossing correction yield the cubic n modulo three coefficient, with no analytic gap requiring numerical extrapolation. The independently implemented checker passed 3065 assertion groups including SymPy expansions and independent Gram reconstruction. The proof, not finite testing, covers all n≥3.

value.rationale: Boundary-arclength least-squares stability is a canonical question in approximating circular interfaces with polygonal meshes. The result has a natural exact infinite family, strict location characterization, a leading positive n^-2 stability defect opposite to the analogous vertex-sampled Fourier projector, and a signed third-order n modulo three distinction caused by zero-crossing locations on edges. These independent parameter effects are not just a known special-case numerical substitution; they sharpen a practical boundary-discretization benchmark.
